verified_claims: Lopez, Matthews & Baumer (arXiv:1701.05976, AoAS 2018), NFL Table 4 checked in the PDF text: γ_season 0.69 (0.042), γ_week 0.978 (0.005), σ_game 0.233 (0.008), σ_season 0.331 (0.019), σ_week 0.147 (0.006). 95% CI for γ_NFL,season is (0.61, 0.77). Glickman & Stern (1998) got 0.99 and 0.82, with an interval of (0.52, 1.28). The data are 10 NFL seasons (2006-2015) of betting-market implied probabilities on the logit scale, fit by Gibbs sampling via rjags.
NFL team-specific vs constant home advantage DIC difference is -153.2 (SE 24.3). This is in the paper's Table 2, not Table 4 as the report implies.
Arithmetic checks out: 0.978 per week gives a half-life of about 31 weeks, and γ_season = 0.69 means about 31% reversion toward the mean.
bigfour/competitiveness exists. It is R/LaTeX research code with rjags models and is licensed CC0-1.0; the report said the license was not checked.
fivethirtyeight/nfl-elo-game forecast.py has HFA = 65.0, K = 20.0 and REVERT = 1/3.0, plus a log(point-differential) margin-of-victory multiplier.
Ash & Adams, 'On Warm-Starting Neural Network Training', NeurIPS 2020: warm-started nets generalize worse than fresh ones at similar training loss.

ADWIN (Bifet & Gavaldà): both ε_cut formulas are quoted correctly from the paper, with m = 1/(1/n0+1/n1) and δ' = δ/n. The paper notes that in practice δ' = δ/ln n is used. Recomputed: the Hoeffding version gives about 0.271 on a [0,1] scale, times 80 = 21.7 points; the Bernstein/normal version with σ = 13.5/80 gives about 0.179, times 80 = 14.3 points. The report's ~22 and ~14 points are correct.

river PageHinkley docs: min_instances = 30, delta = 0.005, threshold = 50.0, alpha = 0.9999, mode = 'both', and the doc says it 'implements the CUSUM control chart'. river is BSD-3 with about 6.1k stars.
Gibbs & Candès (arXiv:2106.00170): the ACI update and the Proposition 4.1 bound (max{α1, 1-α1} + γ)/(Tγ) with probability one are quoted correctly, and the experiments used γ = 0.005.
Giacomini & Rossi, 'Forecast Comparisons in Unstable Environments', J. Applied Econometrics 25(4):595-620, 2010, which introduces the Fluctuation test. Verified via RePEc.
Pesaran & Timmermann, 'Selection of estimation window in the presence of breaks', J. Econometrics 137(1):134-161, 2007. The citation exists; the abstract text was not reachable in this pass.

Davis, Greevy, Lasko, Walsh & Matheny, 'Detection of calibration drift in clinical prediction models to inform model updating', J. Biomed. Inform. 112:103611, 2020: online SGD plus adaptive sliding windows. Verified via Europe PMC.
Dixon-Coles ξ = 0.0065 per half-week (via opisthokonta): ln2/0.0065 ≈ 107 half-weeks ≈ 1 year. The report's ~1 year is correct.
Kish ESS for exponential decay: ESS = 2h/ln2 ≈ 2.885h seasons, so about 780 games for h = 1 at 270 games per season. The derivation is correct.
Power arithmetic for a 5 squared-point degradation, given its stated assumption of SD(model-market) = 2: SD(d) ≈ 54 and n ≈ (2.8·54/5)² ≈ 914 games.
In-repo: server/modeling/registry.js has REQUIRED_GATES = ['schema','leakage','data_quality','baseline_improvement','tests'], promote() and rollback(), and a store-level atomicPromote().

Prior reports say what the report attributes to them. F08 (Koopman & Lit: score-driven beat the state-space model and exponential downweighting, <10 s vs ~1 h; momentumnfl rating_half_life_weeks = 6.0). F04 (Buchdahl: ~50 bets for CLV significance; Hubáček & Šír decorrelation). F07 (Howard et al.: within a factor of 2 of fixed-sample CLT bounds). F11 (marcopeix/conformal-ts, BSD-3, with ACI/AgACI/NexCP).

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: The current gap (14.8 vs 13.55 RMSE, d ≈ 35) would show in about 20 games.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: This mixes incompatible assumptions. If the close is efficient, E[d] = E[(model-close)²], so a gap of 35 squared points means SD(model-market) ≈ 5.9, not 2. Then SD(d) ≈ 2·5.9·13.5 ≈ 160 and n ≈ (2.8·160/35)² ≈ 160-200 games, which is most of a season. Twenty games is wrong by about 10x.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Glickman & Stern: season-to-season SD ~2.35 vs week-to-week ~0.88, so strength moves ~2.7x as much across offseasons as within a season.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Misleading. These are per-transition SDs, and 17 weekly steps compound to about 0.88·√17 ≈ 3.6 points, which exceeds the single offseason 2.35. Lopez's numbers say the same: 0.978^17 ≈ 0.69 ≈ γ_season, so within-season reversion roughly equals between-season reversion. The paper also reports γ_week and γ_season are inversely correlated in the posterior, so they are weakly identified separately. The 2.35/0.88 values are secondhand via F08 and were not re-verified against G&S 1998.

Coincidental agreement on different scales. Elo points with K = 20 and an MOV multiplier are not comparable to market log-odds with a separately estimated γ_week, and the two decays trade off against each other. It is not independent confirmation.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Key finding 2: recursive filtering for team state plus a regularized refit for coefficients beats ad hoc decay (Koopman & Lit 2019).
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Overstated. Koopman & Lit studied soccer and compared a score-driven (GAS) bivariate Poisson against a simulated-ML state-space model and exponential downweighting. They did not test a Kalman filter plus ridge coefficient refit, and GAS is not a Kalman filter. The cited evidence supports score-driven dynamic strength for soccer only.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: For ~270 games per season, a larger γ (0.01-0.02) keeps the ACI bound meaningful within one season (T·γ ≈ 3-5).
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: With α1 = 0.2, γ = 0.015 and T = 270, Proposition 4.1 bounds |mean miscoverage − 0.2| by about 0.82/4.05 ≈ 0.20. That is vacuous for an 80% interval. A larger γ also makes α_t, and so interval width, jumpy. ACI gives no useful within-season guarantee at this sample size; it is at best a heuristic tracker.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: river's adwin, page_hinkley and kswin are each tens of lines to port to JS.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Page-Hinkley and KSWIN are small. river's ADWIN uses an exponential-histogram bucket structure (Cython) and is substantially larger. For ~270 points per season, a naive O(n²) split-check version is fine, so this is minor.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Pesaran & Timmermann (2007) support cross-validated window choice or averaging forecasts across window lengths.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: The citation exists, but the abstract and full text were not accessible this pass, so the content claim is unverified here. It is consistent with the paper's known thrust.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: CLV reaches significance in about 50 bets (Buchdahl, via F04).
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: This is a practitioner claim about price CLV in odds terms, contingent on the true edge size. It is not a peer-reviewed result and not measured for NFL spread CLV in points, so treat it as a rough order of magnitude.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Only 2018+ has opener and snapshot data, giving about 8 seasons for bet-gate training.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Not verified against the database. The brief says game_lines runs from roughly 1999 or 2018 and the quote tape covers recent seasons only, so the bet-gate sample may be smaller than 8 seasons.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: West & Harrison discount δ ≈ 0.98-0.99 per game for the bet-gate regression.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: No source establishes this value for this problem, and the report admits it. It must be a replay-tuned hyperparameter, not a default.

recommendations_to_drop_or_change: Residual-to-market lookahead risk: 'target = margin − closing spread' is fine for training, but mid-week serving happens before the close exists. The served forecast must be anchored to the line available at decision time (or to a forecast of the close), and training for the bet decision should use the decision-time line as the offset. Otherwise it leaks the close. State this explicitly and enforce it with a PIT assertion on the offset column.

Offseason hyperparameter tuning (σ_week, σ_season, γ, HFA prior, λ, half-life grid) must be nested walk-forward. Each evaluated season's hyperparameters may be chosen only from prior seasons. Tuning once on all history and then reporting walk-forward results for that frozen configuration is in-sample selection and will overstate performance. Log every grid point as a trial (F06).

Drop 'the current gap would show in ~20 games'. Replace it with a power calculation that uses the measured SD of (model − market) from game_lines. Expect hundreds of games for anything but catastrophic gaps.
Drop the claim that ACI with γ = 0.01-0.02 gives a meaningful within-season guarantee. Keep ACI only as a heuristic interval tracker, and judge calibration on pooled multi-season data.

Do not import Lopez γ/σ values or FiveThirtyEight constants as priors on the margin scale. Use them only as rough plausibility checks, and re-estimate γ_week and γ_season jointly on margins, noting they trade off.

Per-team home advantage, 32 extra parameters on ~270 games per season: fit only as a hierarchical, shrunk effect around a league mean, never as free per-team parameters. The DIC evidence is from 2006-2015 market log-odds, and league-wide HFA has shifted since.
Soften key finding 2 (Koopman & Lit) to 'score-driven dynamic strength beat exponential downweighting in soccer'. Do not present it as evidence for the specific Kalman-plus-ridge split.

Remove the '2.7x across offseasons' framing. Within-season cumulative drift is comparable to offseason drift, which argues for a meaningful in-season state update, as the report's own loop already does.

Keep the performance-based rollback rule (a confidence sequence excluding zero), but note it will essentially never fire within a season at this sample size. Hard-fault rollback is the only operative in-season mechanism.
corrected_summary:
What survives verification:

**1. How fast NFL strength moves.** Lopez, Matthews & Baumer (AoAS 2018; arXiv:1701.05976; code bigfour/competitiveness, CC0) fit a Glickman-Stern-style state-space model to 10 NFL seasons (2006-2015) of market implied log-odds.
- γ_week = 0.978 (sd 0.005), γ_season = 0.69 (sd 0.042, 95% CI 0.61-0.77).
- σ_week = 0.147, σ_season = 0.331, σ_game = 0.233.
- Team-specific home advantage beat a constant one on DIC by -153.2 (SE 24.3), in Table 2.
- Glickman & Stern (1998) got 0.99 and 0.82.
- Within-season decay compounds: 0.978^17 ≈ 0.69 ≈ γ_season. So in-season and offseason reversion are of similar size, and the two γ's are negatively correlated, so estimate them jointly.
- These are market log-odds values. Re-estimate on margins.
- FiveThirtyEight's NFL Elo (MIT) uses K = 20, HFA = 65, REVERT = 1/3. That is a baseline benchmark, not independent confirmation.
- Dixon-Coles ξ = 0.0065 per half-week implies a half-life of about 1 year (secondhand). momentumnfl's 6-week in-season half-life is via F08. Both are grid candidates only.

**2. Refit cadence.**
- Ash & Adams (NeurIPS 2020): warm-started neural nets generalize worse. It is irrelevant for closed-form ridge or Kalman models, which should simply refit from scratch.
- Update team state recursively after each game. Refit feature coefficients weekly on time-weighted history.
- Freeze hyperparameters in season, but tune them offseason with NESTED walk-forward: each season's hyperparameters come from prior seasons only, and every grid point is logged as a trial.
- Kish ESS for a half-life of h seasons ≈ 2.885h seasons (about 780 games for h = 1). Use multi-season half-lives for coefficients, and consider averaging over several half-lives (Pesaran & Timmermann 2007; citation verified, content not re-read).
- Koopman & Lit (2019, via F08) show score-driven dynamic strength beat exponential downweighting in soccer. That is evidence for dynamic strength, not specifically for a Kalman-plus-ridge split.

**3. Drift detection.** In-season detection is weak at this sample size.
- ADWIN's formulas are quoted correctly. For a half-season split with σ = 13.5, it detects only mean shifts of about 14-22 points, i.e. pipeline breaks.
- The loss differential vs the close needs roughly 900 games to detect a 0.18 RMSE degradation, assuming SD(model − market) = 2.
- Even the current 14.8 vs 13.55 gap needs on the order of 150-200 games, not 20.
- river's PageHinkley is a CUSUM with defaults 30 / 0.005 / 50 / 0.9999 (BSD-3, about 6.1k stars; Python only). Port the logic, set thresholds by replay over historical walk-forward residuals, and run it on weekly aggregates.
- The Giacomini-Rossi (JAE 25(4):595-620, 2010) Fluctuation test is the right offseason relative-performance test.
- Weekly peeking requires anytime-valid confidence sequences (F07: within about 2x fixed-sample width).

**4. Calibration.**
- ACI (Gibbs & Candès 2021) is correctly stated: bound (max{α1, 1−α1} + γ)/(Tγ), with γ = 0.005 in the paper. At T ≈ 270 the bound is vacuous even with γ = 0.02, so use ACI as a heuristic tracker and assess calibration on pooled multi-season data.
- Davis et al. (J. Biomed. Inform. 2020, 112:103611) is a verified clinical precedent for calibration-drift detection that informs retraining windows.

**5. Recommended loop, corrected.**
- Offseason nested tuning, then frozen hashed hyperparameters.
- Per-game state filter with PIT-logged prior and posterior.
- Weekly from-scratch ridge refit of a residual-to-market model with coefficients shrunk to 0. For serving and bet decisions, the offset must be the line available at decision time, never the not-yet-known close.
- Hierarchical, shrunk per-team home advantage.
- Register candidates in server/modeling/registry.js (verified: REQUIRED_GATES, promote, rollback, atomicPromote). Replace the binary baseline_improvement gate with a continuous score.
- Bet gate: a discount-factor regression of (close − bet-time line) on (model − bet-time line), recorded as shadow rows for every game. Stake = fractional Kelly × clipped lower confidence-sequence bound. The discount δ must be tuned by replay. The gate starts at zero given the −2.28 CLV history.
- Hard-fault automatic rollback (NaN, stale data, PIT violation, disagreement blowout, ADWIN/CUSUM alarm) to the market and zero stake. Performance rollback only when a confidence sequence excludes zero, which will rarely fire within a season.
- CLV is the fastest feedback signal. The ~50-bet significance figure is a practitioner claim (Buchdahl via F04).

**Open risks.**
- The shrinkage model may reproduce the market (edge ≈ 0).
- The bet-gate sample may be under 8 seasons; the database was not checked.
- All power figures depend on the unmeasured SD of model − market.
